metrics.label: Brent crude
metrics.blurb: The global benchmark price for crude oil. Most oil cargoes price off it.
metrics.fallback: CNBC live quote, then the daily oil report, then EIA/FRED

metrics.label: WTI crude
metrics.blurb: The US crude benchmark. Its gap to Brent drives US export volumes.
metrics.fallback: CNBC live quote, then the daily oil report, then EIA/FRED

metrics.label: Dutch TTF gas
metrics.blurb: Europe's benchmark gas price, set in the Netherlands.
metrics.fallback: read from the daily European gas report

metrics.label: Henry Hub gas
metrics.blurb: The US benchmark gas price, set in Louisiana.

metrics.label: Coal API2 (ARA)
metrics.blurb: Price of coal delivered into northwest Europe. A dry bulk demand signal.
metrics.fallback: CNBC lists ICE API2 but returns it undated; nothing else free publishes it.
metrics.source: ICE API2 Rotterdam Coal via CNBC

metrics.label: Heating oil / gasoil
metrics.blurb: A refined product price that tracks what bunker fuel costs.
metrics.fallback: CNBC live quote (ULSD heating oil front-month)

metrics.label: RBOB gasoline
metrics.blurb: US gasoline price. Strong margins here pull product tankers west.

metrics.label: Dry bulk ETF (BDRY)
metrics.blurb: An ETF holding dry bulk freight futures. A rough daily read on bulker sentiment.
metrics.source: Breakwave Dry Bulk Shipping ETF via CNBC

metrics.label: Tanker ETF (BWET)
metrics.blurb: An ETF holding tanker freight futures. A rough daily read on tanker sentiment.
metrics.source: Breakwave Tanker Shipping ETF via CNBC

metrics.label: Baltic Capesize Index
metrics.blurb: The Capesize component of the Baltic Dry Index. The most volatile part, and effectively a bet on Chinese steel production.

metrics.label: Baltic Panamax Index
metrics.blurb: The Panamax component. Coal and grain rather than iron ore, so it follows harvests and power demand more than steel.

metrics.label: Baltic Supramax Index
metrics.blurb: The Supramax component. These ships have their own cranes and serve smaller ports, so it reflects broad trade rather than one commodity.

metrics.label: Baltic Dry Index
metrics.blurb: The Baltic Exchange's headline dry bulk freight index. Published late afternoon London time, so a morning brief shows the previous session.
metrics.source: Baltic Exchange via Hellenic Shipping News

metrics.label: VLSFO Singapore
metrics.blurb: Price of the main low-sulphur marine fuel at the world's biggest bunker port.

metrics.label: VLSFO Rotterdam
metrics.blurb: The same fuel in Europe's biggest bunker port.

metrics.label: VLSFO Fujairah
metrics.blurb: The Middle East bunker hub, where most VLCC voyages refuel.

metrics.label: Diesel crack vs Brent
metrics.blurb: Roughly what a refinery makes turning a barrel of crude into diesel. Computed as the gasoil price converted to barrels minus Brent. Fat margins make refineries run hard, which creates product tanker cargo.

metrics.label: Brent–WTI spread
metrics.blurb: How much more Brent costs than WTI. A wide gap makes exporting US crude profitable, which means more long-haul cargoes and stronger tanker demand.

rates.label: Aframax (TD7, N.Sea→UKC)

brief.text:
The lead this morning is military escalation around the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway at the mouth of the Arabian Gulf through which a large share of crude and product liftings pass. gCaptain reports that American warplanes struck an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island on Tuesday. That sits directly on top of the running story of attacks on merchant ships in the same waters, and for anyone fixing Arabian Gulf cargoes it is a war-risk and owner-willingness question before it is a rate question — underwriters price that risk into every voyage quoted through the Strait.

On today's screens, crude is lower: Brent at $92.38 a barrel, down $0.76 or 0.8%, and WTI at $84.59, down $1.42 or 1.7%, leaving the Brent–WTI spread at $7.79. Bunkers — the fuel ships burn — fell with it: VLSFO (very low sulphur fuel oil, the main compliant grade) is $831.50 a tonne in Fujairah, down $29.00 or 3.4%, $862.50 in Singapore (-1.8%), $748.50 in Houston (-0.9%) and $734.00 in Rotterdam (-1.9%). The data here does not show why crude fell on a day carrying an escalation headline; do not assume a link. No freight benchmark has refreshed today. The Baltic Dry Index, which tracks dry bulk rates, stood at 2,893 points on Tuesday 17 November, down 28 or 1.0%; the Capesize index (biggest dry bulk ships, mainly iron ore and coal) was 4,558 on Monday 16 November. VLCC earnings on the Gulf–China route (TCE, or time charter equivalent — daily earnings after voyage costs) were $1,078,714 a day as observed on Sunday 15 November.

Running stories: Hormuz developed today with the Qeshm strike. The Black Sea story also moved — Seatrade reports two merchant vessels sunk off Bulgaria after drone attacks, with seafarers injured and 31 crew rescued. Hellenic reports Week 46 freight weakness spreading to Gulf VLCC routes, with East of Suez ballast counts rising from 415 to 434 vessels. Shadow-fleet sanctions, the Jones Act waiver, Russian diesel restrictions and the suspended US port fees on Chinese-built ships had no fresh news today and are unchanged.

Watch two things. First, whether tanker benchmarks refresh and how they sit against the Hormuz escalation and the building ballaster count. Second, Black Sea grain loadings and insurance terms after two more hulls were lost.

storylines.title: Attacks and escalation around Hormuz
storylines.what: Attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz have continued through November, with two tankers attacked on 16 November. US warplanes struck an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Persian Gulf on Tuesday.
storylines.why_it_matters: Military escalation and hull strikes raise war-risk premiums for Arabian Gulf liftings and shrink the pool of willing owners, reshaping crude and product ton-miles.
storylines.latest: US military strike on an Iranian missile site at Qeshm Island reported Tuesday; separately, Week 46 freight weakness has spread to Gulf VLCC routes with East of Suez ballasters rising from 415 to 434.

storylines.title: Attacks on shipping in the Black Sea
storylines.what: Drone strikes on merchant ships in the Black Sea continue. Two merchant vessels have sunk off Bulgaria after reported drone attacks, with several seafarers injured and 31 crew rescued, following a wheat carrier capsizing earlier in the week.
storylines.why_it_matters: Strikes on ships and port infrastructure threaten grain and dry bulk loadings and add insurance and routing costs for any vessel calling in the region.
storylines.latest: Two more merchant vessels sunk off Bulgaria, seafarers injured, 31 crew rescued.

storylines.title: Sanctions and evasion in the shadow fleet
storylines.what: Sanctions pressure on the shadow fleet is widening, with EU measures targeting shipowners, managers, insurers and financial networks, adding to earlier US designations.
storylines.why_it_matters: Designations force charterers and underwriters to re-verify counterparties, documents and vessel positions, and can strand tonnage outside compliant trade.
sources: How to Reduce False Positives in Vessel Screening Without Missing Real Risk

storylines.title: US Jones Act waiver extended again
storylines.what: A waiver allowing commodities to move between US ports on foreign-flagged ships has been extended for another 90 days, with the pause now past 230 days.
storylines.why_it_matters: It keeps foreign-flag tonnage eligible for US coastwise cargoes, affecting US-flag demand and product tanker employment in domestic trades.

storylines.why_it_matters: Export restrictions and any reopened Atlantic route reshape clean product tanker ton-miles and MR and LR employment.

storylines.what: The US has extended its suspension of port fees targeting Chinese-built and Chinese-operated vessels for another two months while trade talks continue.
storylines.why_it_matters: If reinstated, the fees would change the cost of deploying Chinese-built tonnage into US trades and affect chartering preferences across sectors.
sources: Vestas CEO Calls For EU Crackdown on Chinese Software Used in Wind Sector
